knownLimitation.statement: The defect is established by executed measurement; the remedy is deliberately absent. What is established: the payload is 4,587 bytes over budget at HEAD, projects to 131,991 bytes over at full turnover, the dominant contributor is `tracked` at 72% of a v2 row, the enabling commit is 3855ee75d, and both the 30-row cap and the per-file byte cap are incapable of containing it. What is not established: which remedy to apply, whether candidate 2 can reach the budget by encoding alone, and what per-instrument byte cost is acceptable. Candidate 1 is shown insufficient on its own, landing near 229,841 bytes.

unresolvedFindings.summary: The cockpit first-load payload is 209,387 bytes against a 204,800 budget at 9af68427b, failing 15 selftest assertions.
The overage projects to 131,991 bytes at full recent-window turnover, roughly 29x what is visible today, with no further code change required. This refutes raising briefFirstLoadMaxBytes.

compactRow()'s doc comment holds two documented, deliberate, incompatible intentions: it excludes per-instrument content, and Feature 026 Scope 3 added per-instrument content for the no-refetch property. Neither has been shown wrong.

The retention policy bounds rows (30, which held exactly) but not bytes. briefHistoryRecentMaxBytes is 204,800, identical to briefFirstLoadMaxBytes, so one file of seven may consume the whole payload allowance and the per-file guard can never fire before the aggregate guard.
